justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain ChargeItemDefinition in R6 core as a deprecated or informational resource while steering new work to other financial structures.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves validation and generated-type compatibility, but keeps a rough FMM 0 resource in core and risks indefinite parallel representations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of retiring a draft, FMM 0 financial definition resource is reasonable, especially because the R4 definition says it only provides a rough structure that requires profiling. Keeping the old resource would avoid a hard R4-to-R6 break, but it would also require R6 core and tooling to keep carrying a model HL7 may have decided not to maintain. Because the local inputs do not include official change notes, this is `Probably justified` rather than fully `Justified`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would have left the R4 `ChargeItemDefinition` resource in core with deprecated or informational status and clear guidance not to use it for new designs. That would preserve most R4-valid instances, canonical resolution, package indexes, and generated classes. The material tradeoff is that deprecated resource shapes often persist indefinitely, and R6 would have to support a low-maturity definition resource alongside newer invoice, device, and monetary structures.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a base R6 definitional resource, or a formal successor with applicability and propertyGroup semantics, instead of relying only on Invoice, DeviceDefinition, and MonetaryComponent surfaces.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve reusable billing-rule semantics, but duplicates or competes with R6 transactional charge structures and retains a profile-dependent R4 model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving away from a rough, profile-dependent FMM 0 charge definition resource is a plausible R6 goal. A less-breaking base design could have preserved the reusable applicability and property-group model, but doing so would keep a second definitional representation next to the R6 invoice/device monetary structures and could confuse which representation is authoritative. With no official rationale or successor map in the local inputs, the break is only `Probably justified`, not conclusively justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A StructureMap, ConceptMap, extension package, or local sidecar strategy would be migration mitigation, not a backward-compatible base R6 design. The base-design alternative would be to retain `ChargeItemDefinition` or introduce a formal R6 successor that still carries canonical lifecycle metadata, definition-level applicability, group-level applicability, and grouped price components. That would preserve more R4 content, but the tradeoff is substantial: R6 would have both reusable definition semantics and invoice/device charge representations, and deprecated or duplicate representations can accumulate indefinitely.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `deduction` in the R6 `price-component-type` code system as a deprecated synonym of `discount` while making `discount` the preferred code.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds some synonym-handling and analytics ambiguity, but preserves code-level migration with modest long-term cost.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The terminology simplification is understandable because the R6 `discount` definition explicitly says it may be referred to as a deduction. However, the same goal could likely have been met by retaining `deduction` as a deprecated or synonym code in the R6 required value set while preferring `discount` for new content. A ConceptMap alone would only be migration guidance, but preserving the code in the base R6 terminology would be a real less-breaking design, so this narrower terminology break was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The base R6 alternative would add `deduction` to `price-component-type` with deprecation/synonym metadata and clear guidance that new instances should use `discount`. This would let migrated R4 price components remain code-preserving while still communicating the R6 simplification goal. The tradeoff is moderate terminology clutter: validators and analytics would need to normalize overlapping `discount` and `deduction` codes, and some systems might continue to treat them as distinct.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated core ChargeItemDefinition StructureDefinition so R6 generators can still emit a legacy resource model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces compile-time and parser breakage, but forces R6 core libraries to support an obsolete resource and blurs version-specific conformance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The code generation and serializer break follows directly from removing the core resource. If retiring a draft, FMM 0 resource is accepted as the R6 design goal, then omitting generated support for that resource is probably justified. The alternative is less breaking but not low cost, because it requires R6 core generators, schemas, resource enums, and dispatch logic to keep supporting a resource that the base model no longer wants to expose.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A generated shim or external compatibility package is a useful mitigation but not a backward-compatible base R6 design. The base-design alternative would be to keep a deprecated `ChargeItemDefinition` StructureDefinition in the R6 core package so generators produce a legacy class and parser branch. That preserves source and runtime compatibility for many R4 applications, but it carries obsolete API surface indefinitely and can make it unclear whether accepting the resource is true R6 conformance or legacy tolerance.
